Sue posted and approved 353 of the 373 purchase invoices herself, and the only compensating control is the director's release of BACS runs (FY24-W03). The associate dentist billed 'monthly' fees on only 7 invoices, with none for Apr or Jul-Oct, so unrecorded liabilities could be about 40-50k. Practice Growth Marketing (S009) raised 13 'Website - monthly' invoices, four of them in April alone, plus travel/CPD/rail invoices, and advertising rose 60% on the prior year.

Payroll is identical every month at gross 31,350. The 120 net salary payments on the bank statement go to exactly the 10 employees in the party list, nobody joined or left, and PAYE reconciles: 9,800 + 11 x 11,599.50 = 137,394.50 paid, with 11,599.50 paid on 22 Jan 2026. Segregation is weak because Sue runs payroll, approves the journal and is herself a payee, but the planning match already covers existence. Gross pay is up 5% with no change in headcount, which needs explaining.

There was one addition, the Surgery 2 chair at 45,600 (above PM), which was approved by Raj and paid in full. Depreciation is a flat 2,200 a month manual journal posted by Sue with no approval, contrary to N12 which says Moorland posts it. The total of 26,400 is identical to the prior year, so the new chair has not been depreciated (understatement of about 2-5k, below PM).

All 570 lines on the 2025 statement match the ledger, and the closing 643,933 agrees to TB 1200. However, several flows that should exist do not appear anywhere: no corporation tax payment in 2025, no dividends, and in the Q1 2026 statement no NHS receipts, card takings, January payroll or rent. That suggests either an incomplete statement or another bank account. There is also a manual journal to bank posted by a director.

The known related-party transactions are the two 50% director-shareholders' salaries of 57,720 net each. Two suppliers need corroborating as unconnected: the landlord, which the client asserts is unconnected and is paid 62,400 a year, and Wetherby Dental Laboratory, the largest supplier at 145,655. No dividends or director's loan balance appear in the ledger, and that needs explaining.

This is presumed significant under ISA (UK) 240. The practice is profitable (pre-adjustment profit about 563,600), has cash of 643,933 and no borrowings. The NHS contract runs to at least 2026/27 and the lease to 2031. The only open point is the Q1 2026 statement showing no receipts, which needs explaining before concluding.
No stock account. Dental consumables on hand are immaterial, and the lab work is billed per case.

This is the sixth year with an unmodified prior-year opinion, so OB-01 does not apply. The opening TB agrees to the prior-year closing. However, several prior-year P&L comparatives are identical to the current year to the penny (utilities, professional fees, travel, bank charges, depreciation), so the comparatives column should be agreed to the signed FY2024 accounts during the analytical work.

Last year's file says the practice is exempt and not registered, yet HMRC VAT shows a 'VAT Q4 2025 VAT return' (nil) on 7 Feb 2026, which means a registration now exists. Implants are exempt but cosmetic work (whitening, some implant-adjacent work) can be standard-rated. The ledger codes everything T2/T9 and carries no VAT.

There is no NHS clawback provision (30.6k-61.2k for FY2025 plus whatever 2024/25 needs), no corporation tax liability (about 140k at 25% on pre-tax profit of about 564k, which is a draft figure), and no audit fee accrual (7601 is nil in both years). Accruals of 4,100 have not moved all year, so the prior-year accrual was never reversed and no current one was made. Associate fees for at least 4 months may be missing. Taken together these are several times materiality.

Subsequent events are central this year: the NHS 2025/26 year-end reconciliation (due about July 2026) settles the clawback, and the Q1 2026 bank anomaly needs explaining. Laws and regulations matter too: NHS GDS contract terms, CQC registration and a possible new VAT registration.

keyFindings: There is no NHS clawback provision. 4030 = 1,020,000 = 12 x 85,000 (BK-000001..BK-000034) against delivery of about 92% (N4). The FY2025 share of the 2025/26 shortfall is 30,600 (4% beyond tolerance) to 61,200 (full 8%), against overall materiality of 24,000. The 2024/25 contract-year outcome (Jan-Mar 2025) is unknown: no clawback or recovery appears in the 2025 bank.

The ledger is pre-close: the export of 6 Mar 2026 contains no Moorland journals (moor.accts posted nothing). Corporation tax is nil on the TB and no CT payment went through the bank in 2025 (pre-tax profit about 563.6k, so CT is roughly 140k). The audit fee (7601) is nil in both years, Thornbury (S013) has no transactions, and accruals of 410,000 pence (4,100) are unchanged from opening to closing.

The Q1 2026 statement (B26-00001..B26-00029) shows only payments of year-end creditors and PAYE. There are no NHS receipts on 1 Jan or 2 Feb, no card takings, no January payroll and no rent. Combined with no dividends and no CT payment in 2025, either the statement is incomplete or a second bank account exists.

Private takings stop at CS-000058 (W51, 22 Dec 2025). Nothing is recorded for 23-31 Dec, and nothing is banked in Jan 2026. Implant fees are taken in advance (MJ-000013/B25-00437 refund of 1,900 for 'treatment not proceeding') with no deferred income account.

The associate dentist S016 billed only 7 'monthly' invoices (71,397), with none for Apr or Jul-Oct 2025, while subcontractor cost is +30% on the prior year. That points to possible unrecorded liabilities of about 40-50k, or an undisclosed absence.
MJ-000013 was posted by director raj.md as a manual journal debiting 4040 and crediting bank, with no approver. Raj has no approval limit.

Depreciation MJ-000001..MJ-000012 is a flat 2,200 a month posted by Sue with no approval, contrary to N12 (Moorland). The 26,400 total equals the prior year and does not depreciate the 45,600 chair (PI-000373, May 2025).

Practice Growth Marketing (S009), self-approved by Sue: 13 'Website - monthly' invoices including 4 in April 2025 (PI-000100, PI-000109, PI-000103, PI-000115), plus CPD/travel/rail invoices coded to 7400. Advertising is up 60% (8,786 to 14,057). Several suppliers' invoice narratives do not match their trade (e.g. Clinical Waste Yorkshire billing handpiece repairs, Yorkshire Water billing electricity).
B26-00028 'HMRC VAT, VAT Q4 2025, VAT return' (nil) contradicts last year's note that the practice is not VAT-registered.

Positive results from planning: all 570 bank lines match the ledger and the closing 643,933 agrees to the TB. Every salary payment goes to one of the 10 listed employees. PAYE reconciles to B26-00019. Every purchase invoice over 5,000 was approved by Raj, there is no clustering below the limit, and there are no duplicate invoices. hoursEstimateVsBudget: 60h is not adequate; I estimate 85-90h. Last year the firm budgeted 67h and spent 50h on a clean file with no clawback issue and no REV-06. This year adds REV-04 on the NHS contract (10h), REV-06 on takings (5h, missed last year), REV-03, PUR-03, VAT-01 and BNK-03 (about 11h), plus extended JNL-01, JNL-02, ACC-01 and PUR-05 for a pre-close ledger and an unprovided estimate that is above materiality (about 6h more). Mandatory procedures alone come to about 32h. Do not cut REV-04, ACC-01, JNL-01/02 or BNK-02 to fit; the excess should go to Ingrid as a budget and fee issue, as N10 already anticipates. Savings of about 5h are possible by limiting PUR-03 to two suppliers, relying on the planning bank match for BNK-03, and omitting PAY-03.
